fixes.explanation: That's the job, friend. The LORD says, "Go up this mountain of the Abarim range and see the land that I have given the Israelites." (Numbers 27:12) Notice the word "given." The LORD calls it land He has given to the Israelites, and Moses gets to look at it from up there.

Nope, this verse doesn't mention anyone waiting up there for Moses. The LORD says, "Go up this mountain of the Abarim range and see the land that I have given the Israelites." (Numbers 27:12) What the LORD tells Moses to do on the mountain is see the land. No elders show up in the verse at all.

Ooh, I know why this one sounds right. A leader walks his people all that way, so you expect him to walk in with them. But God doesn't say that. He says, "After you have seen it, you too will be gathered to your people, as your brother Aaron was…" (Numbers 27:13) Seeing the land comes first, then Moses is gathered to his people. I think that's a heavy thing to hear.

Aaron it is. God says Moses will be gathered to his people "…as your brother Aaron was…" (Numbers 27:13) The word "brother" tells you this is family. Aaron comes up again in the very next verse, where God says "…both of you rebelled…" (Numbers 27:14).

Korah is a name that floats up, I get it, but it isn't the one God says here. God says, "…as your brother Aaron was…" (Numbers 27:13) The verse names Moses' brother, so the name has to be Aaron. Korah isn't named anywhere in this passage.

That's it. Moses asks the LORD to "…appoint a man over the congregation…" (Numbers 27:16) He asks this right after hearing he'll be gathered to his people. I think his request shows how much he cares about who leads them next.

Yes, sheep. Moses says he doesn't want the congregation of the LORD to be "…like sheep without a shepherd." (Numbers 27:17) It's a picture of people with no one to lead them. Matthew 9:36 describes the crowds with the same words, "…like sheep without a shepherd."

Soldiers is a fair guess, but it isn't the picture Moses uses. He says he doesn't want the congregation of the LORD to be "…like sheep without a shepherd." (Numbers 27:17) A shepherd is the picture he picks for a leader. I think it's a gentle one.

Spirit is right. God calls Joshua "…a man with the Spirit in him…" (Numbers 27:18) That's the description God gives when He tells Moses to take Joshua son of Nun. Out of everything God could point to, it's the Spirit.

Strength is a natural guess, but it's not the word God uses. He says, "…a man with the Spirit in him…" (Numbers 27:18) The thing God points to in Joshua is the Spirit. The verse never mentions strength.

That's the one. God says, "Take Joshua son of Nun, a man with the Spirit in him, and lay your hands on him." (Numbers 27:18) And Moses does just that. The text says he "…laid his hands on him and commissioned him…" (Numbers 27:23).

A staff handoff would make a great picture, wouldn't it? But the text doesn't say that here. God's instruction is, "…lay your hands on him." (Numbers 27:18) No staff is mentioned in this passage, and hands are what God names.

Right, False. Nothing happens in a back room here. God tells Moses, "Have him stand before Eleazar the priest and the whole congregation, and commission him in their sight." (Numbers 27:19) That's out in the open, with the whole congregation there to see it.

That's the reason God gives. He says, "Confer on him some of your authority, so that the whole congregation of Israel will obey him." (Numbers 27:20) God ties the authority Moses confers to the whole congregation obeying Joshua. Moses gives some of his own, and that's the purpose.

Counsel, you got it. God says Eleazar "…will seek counsel for him before the LORD by the judgment of the Urim." (Numbers 27:21) Eleazar the priest does the seeking, and he does it for Joshua. It all happens before the LORD.

Mercy is a lovely word, but it's not the one God uses here. He says Eleazar "…will seek counsel for him before the LORD by the judgment of the Urim." (Numbers 27:21) The word in the verse is counsel. Eleazar the priest is the one who seeks it for Joshua.

Blessing is a nice thought, but it's not the word in this verse. God says Eleazar "…will seek counsel for him before the LORD by the judgment of the Urim." (Numbers 27:21) The word is counsel. Eleazar the priest seeks it for Joshua.

True. The text says, "Moses did as the LORD had commanded him." (Numbers 27:22) Then it tells what he did: he took Joshua and had him stand before Eleazar the priest and the whole congregation. He had just heard God say he'd be gathered to his people, so I think that's a lot to take in and still do.

This one is True. After God finishes speaking, the text says, "Moses did as the LORD had commanded him." (Numbers 27:22) Then it tells what he did: he took Joshua and had him stand before Eleazar the priest and the whole congregation. After that he "…laid his hands on him and commissioned him…" (Numbers 27:23).
